standard_prerequisites.name: Proper birational morphisms are finite in codimension one
standard_prerequisites.use: Proof lines 3889-3893: a proper birational morphism f : X' -> X is finite and an isomorphism over a dense open.

standard_prerequisites.name: Genus decreases under finite birational maps
standard_prerequisites.use: Proof lines 3893-3894: the inequality dim_k H^1(X, O_X) >= dim_k H^1(X', O_{X'}) follows from this lemma.

standard_prerequisites.name: Sheaves with zero-dimensional support are generated by global sections
standard_prerequisites.use: Proof lines 3901-3904: the cokernel F of O_X -> f_*O_{X'} has zero-dimensional support, hence is generated by global sections, so H^0(X, F) = 0 forces F = 0.

core_obligations: The inequality (proof lines 3889-3894): if f : X' -> X is proper birational then it is finite and an isomorphism over a dense open (Varieties, Lemmas finite-in-codim-1 and modification-normal-iso-over-codimension-1); the inequality dim_k H^1(X, O_X) >= dim_k H^1(X', O_{X'}) then follows from lemma-genus-goes-down.
The equality setup (lines 3896-3900): assume X is reduced; then O_X -> f_*O_{X'} is injective and one obtains the short exact sequence 0 -> O_X -> f_*O_{X'} -> F -> 0.

Rigidity (lines 3900-3907): under the assumptions of the second statement - H^0(X, O_X) -> H^0(X', O_{X'}) surjective and equality of genera - the long exact cohomology sequence gives H^0(X, F) = 0; since F is generated by global sections (zero-dimensional support, varieties-lemma-chi-tensor-finite) this forces F = 0, i.e. O_X = f_*O_{X'}; as f is affine (being finite) this implies X = X'.
proof_roadmap: Use finiteness and dense-open isomorphy of a proper birational morphism to get the genus inequality.
In the reduced case form the exact sequence with cokernel F.
Turn equality of genera plus H^0-surjectivity into H^0(F) = 0, hence F = 0 and X = X'.
difficulty_reason: Rigidity lemma (statement 3878-3887, proof 3889-3907): a birational proper morphism can only decrease the genus, and in the reduced case equality of genera together with surjectivity on H^0 forces the morphism to be an isomorphism - the proof is short and complete, chaining the finite-in-codimension-one property, the genus-goes-down lemma, a long-exact-cohomology computation and the vanishing of a globally generated sheaf with no sections; no verification is omitted. H2: short structural argument.
